recipes.name: Scrambled Egg Brunch Bread
ingredients_raw: 4 ounces thinly sliced deli ham, chopped

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.

Unroll each tube of crescent dough, but do not separate rectangles. Place side-by-side on prepared baking sheet with long sides touching; press and seal seams and perforations. Arrange ham lengthwise down center third of rectangle.
Beat cream cheese and milk in a bowl. Separate one egg, placing egg white aside. Stir egg yolk, remaining eggs, salt, and pepper into cream cheese mixture; fold in red pepper and onion.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat; pour egg mixture into skillet and cook until just set, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and spoon eggs over ham; sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.

Cut 1-inch-wide strips towards the center to within 1/2-inch of filling on each long side of dough. Starting at one end, fold alternating strips at an angle across filling; pinch ends to seal and tuck under. Beat reserved egg white and brush over dough.
Bake in preheated oven until golden, 25 to 28 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Scrambled Egg Brunch Bread
raw_recipe.description: Perfect for brunch, this beautiful braid is filled with eggs, ham, and cheese. Using refrigerated crescent rolls makes it a snap to prepare.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to create this ham, cheese, and egg brunch braid. That's right, breakfast is awesome when it's packaged perfectly and ready to eat on-the-go! This recipe uses refrigerated crescent roll dough to form the crust. Inside is layered with sliced ham, creamy eggs, red bell peppers, onions, and of course Cheddar cheese. Once you've mastered the basics of this brunch bread you'll have to try with all of your favorite fillings or even homemade dough!

review.reviewBody: What a great recipe idea! Saw this and had to modify it to my taste. First, didnt want to make a big one so only used one can of crescent roll dough, then did the ham layer, a couple scrambled eggs (with cheese mixed in) layer and a layer of thawed frozen spinach. Sprinkled some blue cheese along the top and closed it up as directed. Brushed with butter and baked. Wow! What a great breakfast treat, Hubby and I ate all but two slices. I am thinking of several options for the filling that I will try (diced tomatos, olives, mushrooms)-the possibilities are endless. I also am thinking maybe some cream cheese filling with blueberries mixed in to make it into a type of danish. Thanks for posting this great recipe.

I only had one tube of crescent rolls, so just went with it. Cooked bacon first and just sauteed the veggies in the fat with added chopped jalapeno and shallot. Added the egg and cream cheese mix to that till firm. Topped the crescent with diced ham, crumbled cooked bacon, cheese, egg mix , and topped with more cheddar. So good! Will make again! This is great to have in the fridge for hubs to warm up for breakfast!

This turned out to be far more appealing to the eye than the palate. It was beautiful. The exterior was a lovely golden brown and shiny with the egg wash. The interior ingredients were perfectly cooked texturally. The bottom line is ... the taste of the Cresent dough (at least the Pilsbury brand) is far too sweet to complement this savory dish in a pleasingly balanced way. The recipe is worth developing as a sweet dish or suggesting a different crust type (maybe pie dough). Also... a word to the wise...DO NOT prepare this on a 9x13 baking sheet. Two crescent sheets won't fit. Keep the dough fairly chilled, work on parchment paper and transfer to baking sheet on parchment paper for baking.

Good! I used an entire red pepper, an entire bunch of green onions and a lot of Black Forest ham, cut small. I used 2
Pillsbruy Dough Sheets, made it much easier than cresscent rolls. Braiding it was super easy. I did use 8 eggs. Separated the 8th one for the egg white brush. Cooked it 25 minutes on parchment paper.

Long ago introduced to this delicious breakfast served at one of our favorite waterway cafes on its Sunday brunch menu. In spite of halving this recipe since making for two, used about 1/3 cup of peppers (blend of red bell, sweet, and jalapeno peppers). Very versatile dish where other popular breakfast meats can be subbed for the ham (we sometimes use a spicy sausage), and other veggies can be added. The reason for cutting the dough into strips is to eliminate overlapping dough since any underlying layer(s) will have a more doughy texture than the golden brown top layer. Knowing that, you can fold or cut the dough in any number of ways and still get excellent results. We serve this with a homemade finishing sauce. Served alongside some fruit, this makes for an elegant brunch. We would give this more than 5*, if possible. Thank you tiberlady for sharing this fantastic recipe.

I made this with Aldi brand crescent rolls which aren't as nice to work with as the stiffer, Pillsbury brand. I was sure it was going to spring a leak or cook up bad.. but NOPE. Came out PERFECT! I'm not a pepper fan, but my husband LOVED it. I cooked my eggs till I saw no goo.. gooey eggs gross me out. Wrapped it to the best of my ability (accidentally cut the strips all the way to the filling), patched holes where I could see them, brushed it with egg white and shoved it in the oven for 28 mins. The outside was crisp, the inside was perfect. My husband and I were very impressed with the look and overall taste. Next time I am going to try the Pillsbury brand crescents and omit the peppers and green onions. Going to add some crumbled, cooked bacon and sauteed onions to the egg mixture and see how that comes out! Ty for this awesome recipe!

I made one just like the recipe with the addition of some bacon and shallots and without the peppers (I’ve made a ton of breakfast casseroles lately with peppers and my family was kinda tired of them). Amazing. The hit, though, was the one I made with only veggies. I thawed and dried frozen spinach (I would have wilted fresh if I’d had any) and blended that with the egg mixture to cook. I put a very thin layer of cheddar cheese on the pastry dough and spooned the eggs over the top. I sautéed some mushrooms and onions and sprinkled them on the eggs, and I finished with a layer of white sharp cheddar. It. Was. Amazing! The doctors at work at

Great recipe! I used chunky bits of ham not thinly sliced: good idea. I forgot the cream cheese: mistake. Used up some leftover veggies: broccoli, a nice Mexican onion and fresh spinach, adding the last just for a minute or two: great idea. Just cooked the eggs gently to keep them from drying out: good. I had a huge pile of veggies and the pastry strips barely covered them, but that didn't matter. It came out just beautifully and was yummy and healthy though I agree with someone else that the crescent roll dough is too sweet; will try the puff pastry next time. Thanks so much!

The problem that I saw was that there was too much bread. So, instead of using 2 packages, I used one package and rolled it out to the same size (i.e., it covered the bottom of the half sheet pat). It turned out great and there wasn't too much bread. I used bacon (crumbled and cooked almost done), then the eggs. Other than that, I followed the recipe. I will make this again soon.

Freakin incredible. Followed the recipe exact except one thing. Instead of blending the egg/cheese/milk mixture, I put the concoction in the nutribullet and they came out super fluffy. Absolutely delicious. Presents very well. Served my guests with a red fruit salad and mamosas. To die for. Thanks.

Due to time constraints, I put it all together the night before and baked it in the morning. That worked well! It may have taken just a few extra minutes in the oven to compensate for the refrigerator cold. It was received very well by my ladies' group. It was super easy to do as well.
Add Green chili's or roasted poblanos. Filo dough
I didn't add anything this time, but I would more onions and perhaps a bit of Tabasco next time.
This is definitely a keeper! So easy and turns out beautifully. Can’t wait to try other ingredients..gonna let my creative mind come up with other versions!
I love it. Making it again for brunch today. Might add a little Worcestershire for a little zing.
